newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Rockets slam into northern Israel.
newsitem.headline: Rockets slam into northern Israel.

text.p: Katyusha rockets slammed into the Western Galilee region of northern Israel on Friday, the Israeli army and security sources said.
"A number of Katyusha rockets were fired into the Western Galilee tonight at about 8 pm (1800 gmt) from the Qlaileh area of southern Lebanon. There were no reports of casualties or damage," he said.
The rocket salvo was the first such attack against northern Israel since a U.S. brokered ceasefire ended a 17-day Israeli blitz against pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas in April.
Under the ceasefire, the sides agreed not to target civilians. Israel's onslaught was sparked by guerrilla rocket attacks on its northern border towns.

Hizbollah denied on Friday it had launched any Katyusha rockets. Officials of three radical Palestinian guerrilla factions in Lebanon also said they had not carried out any rocket attacks on northern Israel.
The Israeli army said it had not determined who fired the rockets.
On Thursday a five-nation group monitoring the ceasefire said Israeli forces were responsible for shelling two villages last Saturday and deplored the wounding of six civilians in the bombardment.
It was the third time in succession the monitoring group, comprising the United States, France, Israel, Lebanon, and Syria, has held the Jewish state responsible for shelling a south Lebanon village.
The Saturday shelling came after an attack by Moslem guerrillas that killed one Israeli soldier and wounded another.

Israel carved out a 15-km (nine-mile) wide buffer zone in south Lebanon when it withdrew the bulk of its 1982 invasion force in 1985. Israel and the guerrillas have fought each other ever since on the last active Arab-Israeli battlefront.
Israel's overwhelming firepower killed some 200 people in Lebanon, mostly civilians, during the April offensive, dubbed by Israel "Operation Grapes of Wrath."
"Tonight's attack is a blunt violation of the understandings reached as a result of 'Grapes of Wrath'," the army spokesman told Reuters on Friday.
The ceasefire agreement forbids all attacks from or on civilian areas, but does not bar guerrilla raids on Israeli forces in south Lebanon, and gives both sides the right to self-defence.
